name: Baptista Mantuanus
credit: Engraved portrait of Baptista Mantuanus, 17th century (from the Bibliotheca sive thesaurus virtutis et gloriae) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Baptista Mantuanus, born Battista Spagnoli in Mantua in 1447, was a Carmelite friar and one of the most widely read Latin poets of the Renaissance. He entered the Carmelite order as a young man, rose to be its prior general, and died in Mantua in 1516.

His Adulescentia, ten Latin eclogues written in his youth and printed in 1498, treats love, the corruption of the city and court, and the religious life in pastoral dress. The poems became a standard school text across Europe, and in Tudor England Mantuan was read by generations of grammar-school boys.
